Diagnosis: Acute anterior wall ST-elevation myocardial infarction

Procedure Performed: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stent deployment to the Left Anterior Descending (LAD) artery.

Angiography Findings:
Coronary angiography revealed a critical stenosis (95%) of the proximal LAD artery. Other coronary vessels showed no significant disease.

Operative Summary:
Under local anaesthesia and conscious sedation, right femoral artery access obtained. 6F guide catheter positioned. PTCA balloon angioplasty performed. A coronary angioplasty with stent placement was carried out using a 3.0 x 18 mm drug-eluting stent deployed at the site of stenosis. Post-dilatation performed. Final angiography after coronary stent deployment showed TIMI-3 flow with 0% residual stenosis.

Post-procedure Course:
Patient monitored in CCU for 48 hours. Serial ECGs and troponins showed expected evolution. No complications.

Persistent pain and swelling in the left distal femur for 3 months. Progressive in nature.

34-year-old female presented with progressively worsening pain in the left knee region. No history of trauma. Pain is notably worse at night.
Constitutional symptoms reported: mild weight loss (3 kg in 2 months) and occasional low-grade fever.

MRI of the left knee revealed a large aggressive periosteal lesion arising from the distal femoral metaphysis, with soft tissue extension. A characteristic sunburst pattern was noted. These features are highly suspicious for a primary bone malignancy.

Core needle biopsy performed.
Histopathology Report: High-grade conventional osteosarcoma, osteoblastic subtype.

CT Chest: No pulmonary metastases detected.
Bone scan: No distant skeletal metastases.
Current Stage: Stage IIB (Musculoskeletal Tumor Society).
High-grade osteosarcoma of the left distal femur, Stage IIB, non-metastatic. The patient has been informed of the diagnosis of this malignant bone tumor.
The case was discussed at the weekly tumor board. The consensus is for neoadjuvant chemotherapy (3 cycles) followed by limb-sparing resection, and subsequently adjuvant chemotherapy.

Begin systemic chemotherapy as per protocol. Target start date is June 2022. Patient counselled extensively regarding fertility preservation and side effects prior to initiating treatment for this primary bone malignancy.

Osteosarcoma of the left distal femur, post neoadjuvant chemotherapy (3 cycles MAP completed December 2022).
Limb-sparing resection of the left distal femur with endoprosthetic reconstruction.
Histopathological assessment of the resected specimen showed >90% tumor necrosis (Huvos Grade III/IV), indicating good chemotherapy response.

Under general anaesthesia, a medial parapatellar approach was used for this extremity-preserving tumor resection. A wide local excision of the malignant bone tumor with limb salvage was performed. Wide resection of the distal femur (15 cm) was achieved with adequate surgical margins. A modular distal femoral endoprosthesis was successfully implanted. Soft tissue reconstruction was performed and a drain was placed.
Patient remained stable in the immediate post-operative period. Started physiotherapy on POD 2. Wound healing is satisfactory. Drain was removed on POD 3 without complications.

1. Continue physiotherapy as instructed by the inpatient physical therapy team.
2. Adjuvant chemotherapy to begin in 4-6 weeks.
3. Follow-up: Orthopaedic and Oncology OPD in 2 weeks.
4. Serial imaging for surveillance.
Adjuvant chemotherapy (3 additional cycles), followed by surveillance with imaging every 3 months for the first 2 years.
